metadata.description:
What the attachment carries beside its title: the flat `key -> string | number`
object `issue create --meta` writes. Attachments made by integrations may
nest, so it is read as free-form JSON.

prOpenDays.description:
`pr-open-too-long`: a GitHub pull request linked to an issue that has
been open (not a draft) this many days is flagged.

sourceKinds.description:
`source-attachment`: the values `metadata.kind` of a source attachment
may take. Empty: the kind is not checked.

staleDays.description:
`stale-in-progress`: an In Progress issue with no update for this many
days is stale.

statusUpdateDays.description:
`status-update-outdated`: a project's latest status update this many
days old is outdated.

validators.description:
Validator rules to apply to existing issues: the workspace's enabled
rules. `template-sections` needs [`Snapshot::templates`]; an issue does
not record which template it came from, so the closest one is used.

AuditOptions.description: What an audit is narrowed to (`audit --issues KK-1,KK-2 --since <time>`).

issues.description: Issue identifiers, matched without regard to case.

since.description: The time those issues must have been updated at or after.

AuditReport.description: The result of one audit of one workspace.

findings.description: Sorted by rule, then target kind, then target identifier.

unresolvedIssues.description:
Issue identifiers asked for with `issues` that the snapshot does not
contain. They could not be checked, which is not the same as passing.

BuiltRequest.description: What `build_request` returns: where and what to POST.

body.description: The JSON text to send as the request body.

apiCode.description: For a GraphQL error: Linear's own `extensions.code` (`INPUT_ERROR`, ...).

retryAfterSecs.description: For a rate-limit error: how long to wait, if Linear said.

ErrorCodeName.description: The `code` of an error. These are `linear_core::ErrorCode::as_str`.

Failure.description: Why the last refresh failed, and when.

actionable.description:
`true` when the viewer owns the target (leads the project, or is
assigned the issue) and can fix it. Everything else is informational.

fix.description:
A command that fixes it. Placeholders such as `<state>` stand for a
value the person has to choose.

Freshness.description: Whether an entry may be trusted.

oneOf.description: Fetched within the TTL.
Fetched, but longer ago than the TTL: treat as unknown.
Never fetched successfully.

HttpMeta.description: The HTTP facts `parse_response` needs besides the body.

IdParams.description:
An issue, project, milestone or initiative: its id, or for issues and
projects its identifier (`KK-12`, a project slug).

InitiativeDetail.description: What an initiative `view` shows beyond the initiative's fixed fragment.

InitiativeRef.description: A reference to an initiative from a project.

branchName.description:
The git branch name Linear suggests for the issue (Linear's `branchName`).
A branch of this name, or one that holds the identifier, links its pull
request to the issue through the GitHub integration.

prioritySortOrder.description:
Position in a priority-order view, Linear's default (ascending, top first).
`reorder` writes it together with `sort_order`.

sortOrder.description: Position in a manual-order view (ascending, top first). `reorder` writes it.

IssueBrief.description: An issue reduced to what a list inside another entity needs.

IssueDetail.description: What a `view` shows beyond the issue's fixed fragment.

inverseRelations.description: The relations that point at this issue (`blocks`: `issue` blocks this one).

relations.description: The relations that start from this issue (`blocks`: this issue blocks `relatedIssue`).

IssueRef.description: A reference to an issue from another entity.

IssueRelation.description:
A relation between two issues, as Linear stores it: `issue` `type` `relatedIssue`
(`KK-1 blocks KK-2`, `KK-3 duplicate KK-4` meaning KK-3 duplicates KK-4).

IssueStateRef.description: The state of an issue, selected only to count issues per state type.

LabelGroup.description: The group a label belongs to.

MilestoneDetail.description: What a milestone `view` shows beyond the milestone's fixed fragment.

Mine.description: What the viewer looks at in one workspace, as of one successful fetch.

issues.description: Issues assigned to the viewer whose state type is `started`.

newFindings.description:
The findings that were not in the previous snapshot's audit: what a
notifier should report once.

projects.description: The projects those issues belong to.

viewer.description: The authenticated user ("me") in this workspace.

Organization.description: The workspace itself, as Linear names it.

PageParams.description:
One page of a listing. Both fields may be left out: the first page, at the
size that stays under Linear's query-complexity limit for that listing.

first.description: How many items to ask for.

ProjectBrief.description: A project reduced to what a list inside another entity needs.

ProjectDetail.description: What a project `view` shows beyond the project's fixed fragment.

ProjectRef.description: A reference to a project from another entity.

ProjectStatus.description: A project's status (the project-level analogue of a workflow state).

freshness.description:
What a reader should make of the *current* contents, whatever is
decided about refreshing them.

oneOf.description: A reader wants the snapshot (a hook, the statusline, a page load).

A scheduled run. It is a safety net behind webhooks, so it refreshes
once the snapshot is half way to stale.
A verified webhook delivery arrived.
A person asked for a refresh (`linear cache refresh`).

RefreshMeta.description: What is known about a cached snapshot (a cache entry without its data).

failureBackoffSecs.description: Seconds to wait after a failure. Default [`DEFAULT_FAILURE_BACKOFF_SECS`].

fetchedAt.description: When the last *successful* fetch finished. `None`: never fetched.

lastFailureAt.description: When the most recent fetch failed, if the latest attempt failed.

schemaVersion.description: The `schemaVersion` the snapshot was written with.

ttlSecs.description: Seconds a snapshot stays fresh. Default [`DEFAULT_TTL_SECS`].

RefreshReason.description: Why the decision is what it is.

oneOf.description: Refresh: there is nothing cached.

Refresh: the cache was written by a different `schemaVersion`, so it
is treated as missing.
Refresh: a person asked.
Refresh: a webhook says something the snapshot holds changed.
Refresh: the snapshot is older than the TTL.
Refresh: a scheduled run found the snapshot half way to stale.
Leave it: the snapshot is within the TTL.
Leave it: the webhook is about something a snapshot does not hold.
Leave it: the last fetch failed a moment ago; try again later.

Rejection.description: Why a delivery was not accepted.

oneOf.description: The signature is not 64 hex digits.
The signature is well formed but is not the one for this body and secret.
The signature is right but the body is not a webhook payload.
The signature is right but the body has no `webhookTimestamp`.
The signature is right but the delivery is too old (or from the future).

RelationEnd.description: One end of a relation: enough to name the issue and say where it stands.

Rule.description: A validator rule that can be enabled per workspace.

RuleId.description:
Which rule produced a finding. The declaration order is the order findings
are reported in.

oneOf.description: A project's status disagrees with the states of its issues.
A project, milestone or issue is past its target date and still open.
An open issue sits in a project that has milestones, but in none of them.
A project that is not closed has no lead.
An issue has been In Progress without any update for too long.
An In Progress project's latest status update is out of date.
An In Progress issue whose linked GitHub pull request is already merged.
A GitHub pull request linked to an issue has been open for too long.
A validator rule (`template-sections`) applied to an existing issue.
A validator rule (`source-attachment`) applied to an existing issue.
A validator rule (`label-groups-exclusive`) applied to an existing issue.
An issue the caller said it touched was not updated since a given time.
Linear's data is wrong or out of date.
Housekeeping: worth knowing, nothing is broken.

Snapshot.description:
Everything the audit looks at, for one workspace.

`issues` should hold the open issues worth auditing plus any issue whose
state changed recently; the rules only see what is here.

templates.description:
The workspace's issue templates, for `template-sections`. Only needed
when that rule is enabled.

Target.description: The thing a finding is about.

id.description: Linear's id; with the workspace it identifies the target.

identifier.description:
What a person calls it: the issue identifier (`KK-12`), the project's
slug id, or the milestone's name.

url.description: A link to the target (a milestone links to its project).

includeDisabled.description: Also list users who have been disabled.

Verification.description: The outcome of checking a delivery.

WebhookEvent.description: What a verified delivery says about itself.

webhookTimestamp.description: When Linear sent it, in epoch milliseconds.

Whoami.description: The authenticated user and the workspace the credential belongs to.

WorkflowState.description:
A workflow state. Decide on [`WorkflowState::state_type`], never on the
name: names are per-team and renamable, types are not.

WorkspaceCache.description: The cache entry of one workspace.

attemptedAt.description: When the last attempt finished, whether it worked or not.

data.description: The last successful snapshot. `None` while no fetch has ever succeeded.

failure.description: The last failure. Kept until a later refresh succeeds.

fetchedAt.description: When `data` was fetched. `None` while no fetch has ever succeeded.
